children: Soon SpaceX (SPCX, Financials) will find out how much shares investors will buy. Wednesday brings another 319 million shares into play, offering staff and early investors another opportunity to cash out.

That sounds like a lot of possible selling. So far it hasn't worked out that way. Some 912 million shares unlocked Aug. 6, causing the stock to leap more than 6% that day and rise again the next session.
The second test was harder. Another 319 million shares became tradable Aug. 20 and shares plummeted, briefly dipping below the $135 IPO price before recovering.
Now we're in round three. An unlock does not mean all shareholders will sell. It just removes the constraint that they couldn't do that.
The distinction counts because additional 59.1 million shares become eligible Thursday, with more supply still to come.
Wall Street stays constructive. Wells Fargo has a $212 price target, while Pivotal Research recently initiated coverage at Buy with a $220 goal.
Investors care less about Wednesday's price activity than whether heavy insider selling actually shows up.
Another big unlock might be absorbed by demand and start to take some of the edge off the issue of supply post-IPO on the stock.

title: SpaceX Has Survived Two Big Unlocks. The Third Starts Today
